reviews.title: Great app with annoying flaws
reviews.text:
Lots of positive to say. I really think it’s a great app that manages really well to gamify learning a language. I would give it five stars when there wouldnt be annoying und unnecessary flaws:
- Review Dojo: I often get asked the same super basic words like “yes”, “no”, numbers, etc… I must have answered them like 20 times already while I believe I havent been asked 60% what’s in the dojo. I don’t play the dojo every day and I believe the algo seems to reset any progress. It almost makes the dojo useless to me.
- Difficulty: I feel like the app is generally to easy. Sometimes I need to spell a word, but it seems it mostly happens with very easy words and phrases. I feel rarely challenged.
- Point system: Not a big point but I don’t really understand how the point system works. Sometimes I get 80 points for finishing 5 minutes, and right after for the same game I get 300 points.
(happy to increase the rating in the future if things get better)

reviews.title: A great start in many languages
reviews.text:
I want to give five stars—I’ve had this app for 8 years now. But a few things would give it all five: 

1. With gendered languages, they only use one form for things, but inconsistently—sometimes masculine, sometimes feminine. If there are several patterns, you can’t determine the correct way of speaking. While you’d be understood, hopefully, it’s better to learn right the first time. 
2. If you’re not 100% done with a topic, it shouldn’t say that you are. It can leave 3-5 or more words/phrases to do but tell you you’re done with a topic. 
3. The dojo shouldn’t repeat words or phrases that you got right in the same session. If you have 100 words to review in a 5 minute session, repeating ones that you got right is a waste of time.

reviews.text: I LOVED Drops years ago when it was simple, but now the UI is so confusing to navigate. An obscene amount of ads plus AI art… it looks cheap. A pro is that in the Korean section they do provide slightly more in depth grammar lessons now, but they were romanized??? The art to accompany the fill in the blanks was also difficult to see. I was excited to return to Drops but it seems like I’ll be finding something else to accompany my language learning.

reviews.title: Fun supplement with serious flaws
reviews.text: For expanding one’s vocabulary in a language it does ok. But it has the same weaknesses of all the other apps and a few more besides. It is also not keeping up with advances the other apps are utilizing. 1) It doesn’t seem to track real strength or progression. One will be asked to spell a phrase precisely when one has only learned to recognize the whole phrase, but can’t recall parts. Especially tough the farther the language is. 2) No speech recognition. This weak in other apps, but at least they’re trying. 3) No AI.
